clue.text: Hollow place occupied by complete prehistoric creature

parts.note: a hollow in the ground is a dip

indicators.note: a place occupied by something has that thing sitting inside it

parts.note: a locus is a place or position
to do a task is to complete it

explanation.surface: A fossil dinosaur is found lying in a hollow in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complete' looks like an adjective for the creature but is the verb, as in doing a job; 'occupied by' splits the place word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The diplodocus was a huge long-necked dinosaur of the Jurassic period, a prehistoric creature.

clue.text: Imagined country beset by ridicule dismissing leader

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the country goes inside
dismissing leader says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to pillory is to hold up to public ridicule
the US is a country

explanation.surface: A nation imagines itself besieged by mockery after its leader is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: To pillory was to put someone in the stocks for public ridicule; dropping its first letter leaves ILLORY to surround the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Illusory means based on illusion, not real, so merely imagined.

clue.text: Fortune made by patriarch's nephew

definitions.meaning: one's ... is one's fate or fortune in life
in Genesis the patriarch Abraham's nephew is ...

explanation.definitionFit: Lot means one's destiny, and is also the Biblical figure who was Abraham's nephew.

clue.text: Debtor, single person averse to work

parts.note: DR is the accounting abbreviation for debtor
one means single

explanation.surface: Someone in debt is an idle loner.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is an idler who lives off others, like the male bee that does no work.

clue.text: Material presented in two thirds of city clubs

indicators.note: two-thirds of says only the first six of the nine letters are kept

parts.note: Cambridge is an English university city
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Fabric is shown in most of a city's clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMBRIDGE has nine letters; two-thirds of it is CAMBRI, followed by C.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambric is a fine white linen or cotton fabric, a material.

clue.text: Test made unexpectedly available without prescription, price going higher? Crikey!

indicators.note: going higher in a down clue means placed above the next piece

parts.note: SP is the betting abbreviation for starting price
OTC, over the counter, describes medicines sold without a prescription
heck is a mild exclamation like crikey

explanation.surface: A surprise check finds pills sold over the counter, and prices rising, to someone's dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going higher' looks like rising prices, but in a down clue it puts SP above OTC.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot check is an inspection carried out at random without warning, a test made unexpectedly.

clue.text: Absolutely essential to include address

indicators.note: essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction that giving your address is absolutely essential.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead is an intensifier meaning completely, as in dead right or dead certain.

clue.text: Release abuse, upset in social gathering

indicators.note: in says the turned word goes inside the gathering

parts.note: a dance is a social gathering

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to revile is to abuse verbally

explanation.surface: Someone escapes abuse after being upset at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' gives ELIVER, the abuse word turned backwards, and 'in' sets it inside the gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliverance is rescue or setting free, a release from danger or captivity.

clue.text: Grip muscles round body

parts.note: abs are the abdominal muscles
an orb is a sphere, a round body

explanation.surface: Someone grips their stomach muscles round the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To grip a reader's attention is to absorb it, holding it completely.

clue.text: Stand in line in part of ground before start of match

indicators.note: in says the line's letter goes inside the rearranged letters
ground is the past tense of grind, so the words part of are crushed into a new order
start of asks for only the opening letter of the word match

explanation.surface: Spectators queue in one section of a sports ground before kick-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a football ground but is the anagram signal: PART OF becomes PATFOR, with L put inside to give PLATFOR, then M.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand and a platform are both raised structures on which people stand or things are displayed.

clue.text: Solemn buff lacking power to secure wife

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, here by enclosing it
lacking says a letter is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: to buff a surface is to polish it
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A serious enthusiast without influence tries to win over a wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buff' looks like a fan, but it is the verb meaning polish. Taking P away leaves OLISH, and W goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An owl is thought of as grave and wise, so owlish describes a solemn, studious look.

clue.text: Guess when birds should return

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: return says the word for the birds is read backwards

parts.note: emus are large flightless Australian birds

explanation.surface: Someone wonders when the migrating birds are due back.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume is to suppose something without proof, which is to guess.

clue.text: New issue, daft in content? Not at all

indicators.note: new says these letters are given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a silly new edition has anything to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daft' looks like an anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'New' rearranges ISSUE DAFT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsatisfied means discontented, the opposite of content.

clue.text: Rally inside part of Welsh town, unusually

indicators.note: inside part of asks for the town's name without its first and last letters

parts.note: Brecon is a market town in mid Wales
unusually can mean very, as in unusually tall

explanation.surface: A political rally is held in a Welsh town, which is out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' looks like an anagram signal, but it is a plain synonym. 'inside part of' keeps RECO, the town's middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rally is a revival or recovery, as when share prices or a patient pick up again.

clue.text: Exclamation by celebrity about a cell, sadly very plain

parts.note: a cry is a shout or exclamation

indicators.note: about says the celebrity's letters go round the next part

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

indicators.note: sadly means badly or regrettably, so the letters of a cell are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A famous person cries out over a cell that looks bleak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' scrambles the cell's letters and 'about' wraps the celebrity round them with A; the surface makes a sad prison cell, but sadly is only the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crystal clear is perfectly obvious, as transparent as glass, so very plain.

clue.text: Hate plan to imprison knight on island in old, filthy place

indicators.note: to imprison means to shut inside, so the knight goes within the plan

parts.note: to aim is to intend or plan
N is the chess notation for knight

indicators.note: in says the island goes inside the following letters

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, a filthy place

explanation.surface: A loathed scheme jails a knight on an island in a grubby old hovel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just links the two halves; 'in' puts the island inside OSTY, the old filthy place, making OSITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Animosity is strong hostility or ill will, close to hate.

clue.text: Fresher sponge hidden

parts.note: to sponge off others is to beg
inner means inward, kept hidden

explanation.surface: A new student scrounges secretly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresher' is British slang for a first-year university student.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresher, a first-year student, is a beginner at university.

clue.text: Tough country-dweller's family in depression going west

indicators.note: in says the earlier pieces sit inside the depression's letters
going west in an across clue means read from right to left

parts.note: a dent is a small depression in a surface
a hick is a rustic country-dweller, and the possessive gives hick's
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A hardy rural family lives in a hollow that is heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' turns the depression into TNED, and the rustic family goes inside it; hick is mildly mocking slang for a country person.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick-skinned means not easily hurt by criticism, hardened and tough.

clue.text: Wise guy having little prominence outside Washington

indicators.note: outside says the hill's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: a knoll is a small hill, a little prominence
WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington State

explanation.surface: A smart alec has little standing outside Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all is someone who acts as if they know everything, a wise guy.

clue.text: Monarch with mind on making progress

indicators.note: on in a down clue means placed above the next piece

parts.note: to care is to mind
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A ruler is thoughtful about moving ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Career here is the verb, to rush headlong; 'making progress' stands for it loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to move swiftly along, which is a way of making fast progress.

clue.text: Personal training system embraced by Communist leader extremely nobly

indicators.note: embraced by says the first piece is held inside the second

parts.note: Mao Zedong led Communist China
EST, Erhard Seminars Training, was a 1970s personal development programme
so can mean extremely, as in so kind

explanation.surface: A self-help regime is taken up by a Communist chairman in a most noble manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestoso is a musical direction meaning to be played in a stately, majestic way, so nobly.

clue.text: Invention by great chemist

parts.note: an invention can be a made-up story, a lie
great means big

explanation.surface: A notable creation by an eminent scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great' looks like praise for the chemist but gives BIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Justus von Liebig was a celebrated nineteenth-century German chemist, a founder of organic chemistry.

clue.text: Illuminated word used to get attention in print

parts.note: lit means illuminated
ho is a call to attract attention, as in 'land ho'

explanation.surface: A lit-up word is used to grab attention in print.
explanation.definitionFit: A litho is a print made by lithography, printing from a flat inked surface.

clue.text: Sign from one following object of admiration home

indicators.note: following says the one comes after the other pieces

parts.note: a gem is someone or something much admired
in means at home
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A star sign is reached by one tracking a beloved person back home.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the Twins, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Article by doctor comprehended by, very small element

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: comprehended by means contained within, so the doctor sits inside

parts.note: tiny means very small
MO, medical officer, is a military doctor

explanation.surface: A tiny element is described in a paper by a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimony is a metalloid chemical element, symbol Sb.

clue.text: Refuse to go without right coat

indicators.note: to go without means to lack, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: marc is the refuse left after grapes are pressed

explanation.surface: Someone declines to go out without the proper coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun: marc is grape waste. MAC is a raincoat, short for mackintosh.
explanation.definitionFit: A mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh.

clue.text: Reminder for daughter

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

explanation.surface: A note to remind someone, meant for a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A prod is a nudge or prompt, a reminder to do something.

clue.text: Old lawyer in action retaining constant caution

indicators.note: retaining means holding within, so the constant goes inside
in action means at work and moving about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
C is the scientific symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A veteran solicitor in court keeps a steady caution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in action' rearranges the first two words into YELLOWARD; 'retaining' holds the constant inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a yellow card is shown by the referee as a formal caution to a player.
